newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy govt calls second confidence vote on decree.
newsitem.headline: Italy govt calls second confidence vote on decree.

text.p: Italy's centre-left government has called a confidence vote in the upper house of parliament (Senate) on a decree covering changes to the transport sector, Transport Minister Claudio Burlando said on Tuesday.
Burlando said the vote would be held on Wednesday. Prime Minister Romano Prodi's cabinet won a similar motion on the same decree in the lower house last week.
The centre-left government relies on support from the hard-left Communist Refoundation party for its majority in the lower house but controls the Senate without outside backing.

The government has resorted to numerous confidence votes during its 10 months in office after a Constitutional court decision banning the cabinet from the traditional practice of re-issuing old decrees.
Under the new system, a cabinet bill automatically expires after 60 days unless passed into law by parliament. The transport decree is due to expire on Wednesday.

The centre-right opposition wants to change the bill, which will reform the fiscal system for the sector and cut the number of motorway tariffs for haulage companies, but Burlando told the Senate there was not enough time to debate the amendments.
